answer_text:
Let \(r=\frac13\). First compute the unrestricted triple sum:

\[
T=\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^{i+j+k}
=\left(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} r^n\right)^3
=\frac{1}{(1-r)^3}
=\frac{27}{8}.
\]

Interpreting \(i\neq j\neq k\) as “\(i,j,k\) are pairwise distinct,” we subtract the cases where at least two indices are equal using inclusion–exclusion.

For a specific equality, say \(i=j\):

\[
E=\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^{2i+k}
=\frac{1}{1-r^2}\cdot \frac{1}{1-r}
=\frac{9}{8}\cdot \frac{3}{2}
=\frac{27}{16}.
\]

There are \(3\) such equality cases.

For all three equal, \(i=j=k\):

\[
F=\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} r^{3i}
=\frac{1}{1-r^3}
=\frac{27}{26}.
\]

Thus the sum over pairwise distinct \(i,j,k\) is

\[
S=T-3E+2F
=\frac{27}{8}-3\cdot\frac{27}{16}+2\cdot\frac{27}{26}
\]

\[
=\frac{27}{8}-\frac{81}{16}+\frac{27}{13}
=\frac{81}{208}.
\]

So, under the pairwise-distinct interpretation,

\[
\boxed{\frac{81}{208}}
\]

27B·v4.method: Inclusion-exclusion on the unrestricted geometric sum, subtracting equality cases to enforce pairwise distinct indices.
